title: VUA packages-repo-catalog result v0.1
description: Result documents for the packages-repo-catalog v0.1 read face (proposal 027 F2 freeze batch 2026-09-20; core rulings 58d1a0c / environment verification 3bd4f12 / desktop stance 75f0dac). The envelope mirrors the standing wire shape (schemaVersion/operation/result): the envelope const is the word-list-row family version 0.1; the result document carries its own family const vua.packages-repo-catalog/v0.1 — two independent versions (the c914cf2 standing rule). The result groups the installable-package inventory PER REPOSITORY: each repo row projects the library's repository identity facts verbatim (repoId and name are nullable — null is the honest projection of the library Option, never padded), carries the REQUIRED per-repo cache-hit fact cached (true = a refreshed local cache inventory exists for this repository, false = subscribed but never refreshed — its own honest state rendered with an EMPTY packages array, never hidden, never rendered as an error), and lists that repository's own package rows in the repository cache's own entry order (no invented sort keys; consumers impose their own presentation order and machine-read by packageId). A package present in several repositories appears UNDER EACH repository that carries it — this face never merges repositories (the cross-repository latest judgment is the packages-catalog family's declared fact; the two views are different and both are honest). cacheSourced is the REQUIRED informational degradation-disclosure fact born with this v0.1 (the packages-catalog v0.2 precedent adopted at birth per the 027 core ruling): true = THIS result was served through the cache-degradation path (offline -> load_cache, or an online load failed and degraded — the ORC-ADP-006 isomorphic precedent), false = served from an online-refreshed load; cache sourcing is NOT an error — consumers render it as an informational 'cached data' annotation, never a failure. Package rows stay inside the library's ACTUAL field ceiling (proposal 027 F2 wording: 'meta information at the library's actually-available ceiling'): packageId (the manifest name), displayName (nullable; null renders the packageId as the display name, P1 ruling 3), description (nullable honest absence), latestVersion (the frozen per-repo judgment: the repository's own newest version that is neither yanked nor excluded by the user's show_prerelease_packages server-side setting, evaluated with NO project Unity constraint — null when no version qualifies under the current setting; absence is not 'no packages'), and versionCount (the repository cache's own inventory count of version entries, yanked included — the cache fact, not an availability promise). AUTHOR IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT: the library's PackageManifest deserialization closed set carries no author field and drops undeclared keys (environment verification 3bd4f12 s1(b): the macro structure, serde behavior, and the sample-JSON-with-author evidence), so v0.1 rules the honest-absence option (iii) — a second parsing surface over the raw cache JSON was REJECTED to keep one fact source; a row carrying author (or license/changelogUrl/downloadCount or any other invented fact) is INVALID by schema, not merely discouraged (false-assertion guard, P1 additionalProperties discipline). There is deliberately NO compatible field on this face: without a project context the compatibility judgment cannot execute and a constant null is not a fact; per-package version-level compatible remains the packages-catalog face's project-bound frozen fact. An EMPTY repos array is a valid, honest answer (zero repository caches); an empty packages array on a cached row is the honest answer for a filter that matches nothing — the filter is a lens, never an existence assertion, so vua.vpm.no_matching_package has NO reach on this face (declared in the protocol document).

repos.description: Per-repository inventory rows in the collection's own enumeration order (predefined official/curated per the library load order, then subscribed user repositories in subscription order — projected verbatim, no invented sort keys). EMPTY = honest zero-repository-caches answer.

cacheSourced.description: REQUIRED informational degradation disclosure (born with v0.1, packages-catalog v0.2 precedent): true = this result was served through the cache-degradation path (offline -> load_cache, or online load failed and degraded); false = served from an online-refreshed load. Informational, never an error: consumers annotate 'cached data', they never render it as a failure.

repoId.description: Repository identifier; null when the library carries none (honest Option projection, never padded).

name.description: Repository display name; null when the library carries none. The consumer falls back to repoId for presentation, never to an invented label.

cached.description: Per-repo cache-hit fact: true = a refreshed local cache inventory exists; false = subscribed but never refreshed (honest listed state rendered with an empty packages array, never hidden, never an error).

packages.description: This repository's own installable package rows in the repository cache's own entry order. EMPTY on an uncached repo (honest), or when the packageIds filter matches nothing here (the filter is a lens, never an existence assertion).

packageId.description: The VPM package identifier (the manifest name).

displayName.description: The package's display-name fact; null renders packageId as the display name (P1 ruling 3), never posing as field fact.

description.description: The package description fact within the library's field ceiling; null = the manifest carries none (honest absence, never padded).

latestVersion.description: Frozen per-repo judgment: this repository's newest version that is neither yanked nor excluded by the user's show_prerelease_packages server-side setting (NO wire switch — no invented preference field), evaluated with NO project Unity constraint. null = no version qualifies under the current setting; absence is not 'no packages' and never renders as an error.

versionCount.description: The repository cache's own inventory count of the package's version entries, yanked included — the cache fact as counted, not an availability promise.
